clue.text: Do get a line reconnected to the embassy

indicators.note: reconnected means these words' letters are joined up again in a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction to restore a telephone line to the embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconnected' signals rearranging the letters of DO GET A LINE. The telephone surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a body of envoys sent abroad, which is a delegation in the diplomatic sense.

clue.text: Upset lunatic English lady

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word above is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: lunatic as an adjective means mad

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman who is mentally disturbed and distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' in a down entry means read upwards; 'lunatic' looks like a noun describing the lady but supplies the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A dame is a woman of rank or, more loosely, any lady, as in the honour title.

clue.text: Not a long distance visit to the pub

explanation.surface: A short trip down to the pub is hardly a long-distance journey.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a telephone call within the local area; the other reads 'local' as a British pub near home and 'call' as a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-range phone connection is not long distance; dropping in at your nearby pub (the local) is paying it a call.

clue.text: One turns up in Georgia for Italian port

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the abbreviation for the US state

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone appearing in Georgia, though bound for a port in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses ONE to give ENO, which goes 'in' GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a major seaport on the north-west coast of Italy.

clue.text: Part of plant needing to burrow after water source

indicators.note: after places the digging word behind the water word in the answer

parts.note: a tap is a source of water
to root is to dig or burrow, as a pig does

explanation.surface: A plant part that has to dig down towards where the water comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'water source' sound like groundwater a root seeks, but it is the household fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproot is the main central root growing straight down from a plant.

clue.text: A poet is disposed to acquire drugs

indicators.note: disposed here means arranged differently, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A poet inclined to take drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges A POET IS. 'is disposed to' reads as 'is inclined to', hiding the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotic drugs derived from opium.

clue.text: Signal for Morse to make a quick move

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse is told to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse code uses dots and the longer signal; the surface suggests the TV detective Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Morse code the long sound is one of its two signals; to rush somewhere quickly is to sprint off.

clue.text: A man with commercial support is way out front

indicators.note: support in a down clue means this piece sits underneath the others, holding them up

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
an ad is a commercial, a television advertisement

explanation.surface: A man backed by sponsorship is well in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' places AD below A HE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well in front, leading the field, is being in advance of everyone.

clue.text: Bad luck if it's Parmesan

explanation.surface: A remark about the cheese on offer being Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase means 'tough luck'; the second reading is literal, since Parmesan is a famously hard cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is British slang for misfortune; Parmesan is literally a firm, aged grating cheese.

clue.text: Soothing influence of speech in royal residence

parts.note: balm is anything soothing or healing
oral means spoken, relating to speech

explanation.surface: Calming words spoken in a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the British royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is a Scottish home of the British monarch.

clue.text: Burgundy is clearly expecting rain

explanation.surface: A Burgundy wine that is evidently anticipating wet weather.
explanation.walkthrough: MACON is a wine from Burgundy; read as MAC ON, someone wearing a mackintosh (a raincoat) is clearly expecting rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a wine region and wine of southern Burgundy; wearing a raincoat shows one anticipates showers.

clue.text: Soldier has little hesitation in becoming a sea dog

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A soldier who hardly hesitates in turning sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: A privateer was a privately owned ship, or its captain, licensed to attack enemy shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old sailor or pirate, and a privateer was a licensed sea raider.

clue.text: Tidy up and leave

explanation.surface: Clean the place and then go.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough tidying is a purge of clutter; to depart quickly is to clear off.

clue.text: I object to little medical man taking wine

parts.note: me is the object form of I
doc is a short informal word for a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that a junior doctor is drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' looks like a protest but is grammar: ME is the objective case of I.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the region of that name.

clue.text: Having started Germany's conversion to the ecu?

explanation.surface: A question about Germany switching currency to the European unit.
explanation.walkthrough: To be off the mark is to have got started; Germany's currency was the Deutschmark, so converting to the ecu took it off the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having begun scoring or moving; abandoning the Deutschmark literally moves Germany away from that currency.

clue.text: A priest with nothing is under great stress

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a title for a priest
aught, a variant of ought, is an old word for zero or nothing

explanation.surface: A priest left with nothing is badly stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: AUGHT usually means 'anything', but as a variant of OUGHT (nought) it can mean zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught describes a person or situation full of anxiety and tension.

clue.text: US serviceman's ball incorporates universal counselling

indicators.note: incorporates means the other piece is taken into the body of these letters

parts.note: GI is the name for an American soldier
U is the film certificate abbreviation for universal
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An American soldier's dance includes advice for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporates' puts the universal letter just after the first letter of the soldier's abbreviation; 'ball' is the dance, not a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidance is advice or counselling given to help someone decide.

clue.text: To provide lunch about 1.50 is obsequious

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the meal word goes round the numbers

parts.note: to serve is to provide a meal
1 is I and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Serving lunch at ten to two is fawning behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.50' looks like a time but is Roman numerals I and L, which SERVE goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Servile behaviour is excessively eager to please, slavish and fawning.

clue.text: Wild eglantine is not cultivated

indicators.note: wild means disordered, so the letters of the rose name are scrambled

explanation.surface: Wild sweetbriar has not been grown in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Eglantine is a wild rose, sweetbriar; 'not cultivated' suggests gardening but means lacking refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or refinement, the opposite of a cultivated manner.

clue.text: Territorials left Defence Minister giving a lecture

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
Tom King was the UK Defence Secretary around 1990

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers leave the Defence Minister to address them.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is Britain's army reserve; Tom King was the Conservative Defence Secretary when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking to an audience, as in delivering a lecture, is addressing them in words.

clue.text: 1000 dollars given to less diligent window installer

parts.note: G, short for grand, is slang for a thousand dollars
lazier means less hard-working

explanation.surface: Paying a thousand dollars to a slacker to fit a window.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'grand' is a thousand, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a tradesman who cuts and fits glass panes into windows.

clue.text: Brief letters from military quarters

explanation.surface: Short notes sent from army barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: A billet is an old word for a short note (as in billet-doux), and also lodging for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Billets are short notes, as in the French love note, and also soldiers' lodgings.

clue.text: Nothing in north London borough for a titled man

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the name of the borough

parts.note: Barnet is a borough in north London
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing in a north London suburb suits an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is a London borough on the city's northern edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title ranking below a baron.

clue.text: Heath and I meet Conservative in time

indicators.note: in places the pair inside the word for a period

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Ted Heath and I meet a Tory in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' suggests the Conservative prime minister Edward Heath, but it is the plant: erica is the heather genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, low shrubs of moorland.

clue.text: Pakistani banker from Indiana, America

parts.note: Ind is an abbreviation for the US state of Indiana
US stands for America, the United States

explanation.surface: A financier from Pakistan who hails from Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword trick: something with banks, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is the great river flowing through Pakistan, so it has banks.

clue.text: Retired painter took it easy and stopped

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the artist's letters are turned round

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
rested means relaxed or took it easy

explanation.surface: A retired artist relaxed and gave up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns RA into AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested means halted or brought to a standstill, as in arrested development.

clue.text: Diving equipment for young scout in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the junior scout inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: a cub is a junior member of the Scouts

explanation.surface: Gear for a junior scout going diving in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba is the self-contained breathing apparatus used by underwater divers.

clue.text: Lady accommodates one who succeeds

indicators.note: accommodates means takes in, so the numeral goes inside the pronoun

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a lady
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lady takes in a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' gives I to HER and also reads into the definition 'one who succeeds'.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who inherits or follows another in a title or estate.

clue.text: Craving post-Christian clarity of speech

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, dates years after the birth of Christ
diction is the clarity of one's pronunciation

explanation.surface: A longing for the clear articulation of a modern era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post-Christian' looks like a religious term but means AD, years after Christ's birth.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive need or craving for something.

clue.text: States how old one is. It's the custom

parts.note: US stands for the United States
age is how old a person is

explanation.surface: A form asks how old you are; this is the usual practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a verb but is the noun US.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established practice or custom.

clue.text: X is found in potassium and sulphur

indicators.note: found in means the short word lies inside the pair of symbols

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about where an unknown element is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X' suggests an unknown in science but is the cross written as a kiss at the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An X at the end of a letter stands for a kiss.

clue.text: It gives the angle in favour of farm vehicle

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone backing a farm vehicle has an angle on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is a semicircular instrument used to measure angles.
